solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Just when pearl of wisdom can be testing?

parts.note: 'as' can mean 'just when', as in 'as the bell rang'
a pearl of wisdom is a wise remark, a saying or maxim

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a nugget of wisdom, offered at just the right moment, might put a person to the test.
explanation.definitionFit: Assaying is analysing metal or ore to judge its quality, a kind of trial or examination.

clue.text: Starting point for endeavour in which maybe four succeeded, reportedly?

indicators.note: reportedly means the phrase is to be heard spoken rather than read as spelt

parts.note: four is an example of a square number, and succeeded means won, so said together these give a phrase that sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: It sounds like a sports report about a team of four that managed to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks four as just one example of a square number.
explanation.definitionFit: To go back to the very beginning of a project is to return to this idiom's starting point, borrowed from board games.

clue.text: Game leader departing with a word of appreciation in Asian city, once

indicators.note: the leader of the game's name, its first letter, departs from it

parts.note: halma is a board game where pieces jump across a square board
ta is a British informal word for thank you

explanation.surface: A game captain leaves with a brief thank-you, somewhere in Asia long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is everyday British slang for thanks. Halma is a board game, a forerunner of Chinese chequers.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma-Ata was the former name of Almaty, the largest city in Kazakhstan, so it is an Asian city of the past.

clue.text: Group of jolly dimwits set up a happy scene

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the letters are raised, read from bottom to top
a group of letters is taken from inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A cheerful band of fools stage a contented tableau.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group of' picks LLYDI out of jolLY DImwits; 'set up' turns it to read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An idyll is a peaceful, pleasant picture of rural or simple life, a blissful scene.

clue.text: Superior-sounding female set

indicators.note: this is how the word for a young woman sounds when said in a posh, upper-class accent

parts.note: a female, a young one, is a girl

explanation.surface: A woman with a lofty voice settles into place.
explanation.walkthrough: Upper-class British speech famously renders 'girl' as 'gel'.
explanation.definitionFit: To set, as jelly does, is to become firm, which is what a liquid does when it gels.

clue.text: Seabird leaving home has little hesitation to get fish

indicators.note: leaving says the following word is taken away from the bird

parts.note: the puffin is a seabird with a bright beak
in means at home
er is a short pause sound made while hesitating

explanation.surface: A seabird leaves the nest, pausing slightly before catching a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A puffer is a fish that inflates itself when threatened, also called a blowfish.

clue.text: Put on airs ridiculously, like a French author

indicators.note: ridiculously says the preceding words' letters are arranged absurdly into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is accused of putting on absurd airs, in the manner of a French writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Marcel Proust was a French novelist; the adjective describes something in his style or manner.

clue.text: United around military leader and single-minded

indicators.note: around means the first word's letters go around the second's

parts.note: joined together, as metals are fused
OC is the abbreviation for Officer Commanding

explanation.surface: A team rallies round its commander, with one purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: A focused person concentrates on one aim, the same as being determined on a single goal.

clue.text: Register of leaderless soldiers with inadequate function

indicators.note: leaderless means the first letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: soldiers are men in the ranks

indicators.note: inadequate means the word falls short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a function is a role, a job something does

explanation.surface: A roll call of soldiers without a commander, who can barely do their job.
explanation.definitionFit: To register is to sign up formally, as a student does at a college.

clue.text: Attack from the rear to capture a Pacific island

indicators.note: to capture means the reversed word holds the following letter inside it
read from the rear means the word goes backwards

parts.note: to mug is to attack and rob

explanation.surface: An assault from behind seizes a South Seas territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Guam is a US territory in the western Pacific, an island in Micronesia.

clue.text: Shout with pain, with heart maybe leading to caution in game

parts.note: to yell is to shout
ow is the cry made in pain
a heart is one example of a playing card

explanation.surface: A footballer yelps in pain, perhaps from a heart problem, and gets booked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart maybe' signals an example: a heart is a card from that suit.
explanation.definitionFit: In football a referee shows this coloured card to warn, or caution, a player for an offence.

clue.text: Superior one joining up with four others

definitions.text: Superior one joining up with four others

parts.words: Superior one joining up with four others
parts.note: Lake Superior is one of five connected North American lakes, linked with Michigan, Huron, Erie and Ontario

explanation.surface: A senior officer teams up with four colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: The five linked freshwater lakes of North America include Superior, the largest, joined to four more.

clue.text: Fired-up type, source of illumination

parts.note: a kind is a type or sort
an LED, light-emitting diode, is a source of light

explanation.surface: An excitable sort of person turns out to be a bright spark.
explanation.definitionFit: Something kindled has been set alight, so it is fired up, literally or with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Mood of small son confronting 'umungous lout?

indicators.note: confronting means the first piece stands facing, so before, the next

parts.note: S is the short form of son

indicators.note: the dropped h shown by the apostrophe tells us to drop the H from the word for a huge lout

parts.note: a hulk is a big clumsy lout

explanation.surface: A little boy squares up to a massive thug while in a bad temper.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in ''umungous' mimics a dropped H, Cockney style, so HULK loses its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A sulk is a fit of sullen, resentful bad temper, a mood in the sense of a huff.

clue.text: Turn of old French actor performing after end of war

indicators.note: after says these pieces follow the next one
end of means the final letter of the next word

parts.note: Jacques Tati was a French comic actor and director
on stage means performing, so 'on'

explanation.surface: An elderly French film star appears on stage once the fighting is over.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotation is a single complete turn about an axis, or a turn in a rota.

clue.text: This writer's means of communicating with article heartlessly direct

parts.note: the setter refers to themself: this writer is I, so this writer's is I'm
the media are means of mass communication

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter is removed

parts.note: the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A columnist muses on how plainly they talk to the press, with a cold-hearted piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This writer's' reads as I'M, I am.
explanation.definitionFit: Immediate contact is direct, with nothing in between, as in an immediate superior.

clue.text: Something very cold about lord close to you, dictator

indicators.note: about means the cold word goes around the next pieces

parts.note: ice is something very cold

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A frosty aristocrat sidles up to a tyrant.
explanation.definitionFit: Il Duce, 'the leader', was the title used by Benito Mussolini, Italy's fascist dictator.

clue.text: Criminal, in my opinion, had finally obeyed the law?

parts.note: a con is a convict, a criminal
'for me' means as I see it, in my opinion

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A speaker reckons a convict finally went straight.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: conforming is complying with any rule, not just law.
explanation.definitionFit: To have conformed is to have complied with rules or standards, behaving as required.

clue.text: Once in a blue moon, old master goes wrong, turning out bad art

indicators.note: goes wrong means the letters of the old master are muddled
turning out means some letters are thrown out of the mix, here those of the word art

explanation.surface: An art critic complains a classic painter has gone off, producing poor work.
explanation.walkthrough: Mix OLD MASTER, then take out the letters of ART ('turning out bad art', bad also a hint the art is scrambled): six letters are left to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Something happening once in a blue moon happens rarely, hardly ever.

clue.text: Heading north, attacked to achieve rescue

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to have reviled someone is to have attacked them in words

explanation.surface: A northbound force, having struck, completes a rescue mission.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from danger is to save or set them free.

clue.text: Light piece of verse that facilitates communication

parts.note: to light is to land or settle, as a bird lights on a branch
a line is a piece of a poem

explanation.surface: A short, lightweight poem helps people get in touch.
explanation.definitionFit: A fixed wired telephone connection is one means of keeping in contact by phone.

clue.text: Girl seeing bird, one in meadow

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the meadow word

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a poetic word
the tit is a small bird
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A young woman spots a small bird out in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: Letitia is a female first name, so it fits any girl.

clue.text: Acknowledge hospital is having trouble

parts.note: H is the map abbreviation for hospital
to ail is to be in trouble or unwell

explanation.surface: A notice admits the hospital is struggling.
explanation.definitionFit: To hail someone is to greet or salute them, recognising their presence.

clue.text: Leading character abroad captured by female photographer

indicators.note: captured by means the letters are held within the following words

explanation.surface: A foreign leading man is snapped by a woman with a camera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading character' suggests a star, but it is the first letter of an alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, a leading letter from another language.

clue.text: One addict, I fancy, could show this

definitions.text: One addict, I fancy, could show this

indicators.note: fancy used as a verb means imagine, but here it says the letters are dressed up into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A speaker suggests that a habitual user would display commitment.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: an addict shows devotion to their habit.
explanation.definitionFit: An addict is wholly committed to a habit, showing steadfast devotion, if of a dubious kind.

clue.text: Game with boxes, present finally emerging

indicators.note: emerging means that letter comes out of the boxes word

parts.note: chests are large boxes

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of the next word

parts.note: taken as written, only its last letter is used

explanation.surface: A game comes in a box, with the gift finally unwrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Chess is a board game for two players.

clue.text: Have nothing to do with hermit-style holiday?

parts.note: leave is time off work, a holiday
a hermit lives alone

explanation.surface: Someone wants no part in a solitary getaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay reads as 'leave alone', a holiday taken solo like a hermit.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun or not interfere with something is to keep away from it entirely.

clue.text: Funny comedian ignoring the first of three daughters

indicators.note: the comedian's name contains three of the letter for daughter; ignoring the first one means dropping it

parts.note: Ken Dodd was a famous British comedian from Liverpool
D is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A comic disregards the eldest of his three girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Dodd was a long-running British stand-up comedian. His name has three Ds; drop the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny can mean strange or peculiar, as in 'a funny feeling'.

clue.text: Abdomen, soft little protuberance

parts.note: tum is an informal word for stomach or abdomen
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A doctor notes a small soft swelling on the belly.
explanation.definitionFit: A tump is a small mound or hillock, a dialect word for a rise in the ground.

clue.text: Load of church silver, holy books missing

indicators.note: missing means those letters are taken out of the silver word

parts.note: argent is silver in heraldry
NT, the New Testament, is a set of holy books

explanation.surface: A church's silver plate is heavy, but the bibles have gone.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a load, as the charge of powder put into a gun or a burden laid on someone.

clue.text: The old man's entertaining celebrity baddies

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the next word inside, as a host holds guests

parts.note: the old man is slang for father, dad, so the old man's is dad's
a star is a celebrity

explanation.surface: Father is hosting a famous guest, and they are villains.
explanation.definitionFit: Dastards are despicable cowards or villains, an old-fashioned word for rotters.
